result.topic_en: Transformation of the hydrodynamic equations of motion for the rotating fluid ellipsoid into moving coordinates ξ, η, ζ via a time-dependent orthogonal transformation (α, β, γ, ...), with the derivation of auxiliary relations among the derivatives of the direction cosines.
result.transcription:
2.
Offenbar ist es erlaubt, in jenen Gleichungen, statt der Derivirten nach den Anfangswerthen der Grössen x, y, z, welche dort durch a, b, c bezeichnet sind, die Derivirten nach den Grössen $\xi, \eta, \zeta$ zu setzen; denn die hiedurch gebildeten Gleichungen lassen sich als Aggregate von jenen darstellen und umgekehrt. Wir erhalten dadurch, wenn wir für $\frac{\partial x}{\partial \xi}, \frac{\partial y}{\partial \xi}, \ldots, \frac{\partial z}{\partial \zeta}$ ihre Werthe einsetzen
$\frac{d^2x}{dt^2}\alpha + \frac{d^2y}{dt^2}\beta + \frac{d^2z}{dt^2}\gamma = \varepsilon\frac{\partial V}{\partial \xi} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial \xi}$
(1) $\frac{d^2x}{dt^2}\alpha' + \frac{d^2y}{dt^2}\beta' + \frac{d^2z}{dt^2}\gamma' = \varepsilon\frac{\partial V}{\partial \eta} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial \eta}$
$\frac{d^2x}{dt^2}\alpha'' + \frac{d^2y}{dt^2}\beta'' + \frac{d^2z}{dt^2}\gamma'' = \varepsilon\frac{\partial V}{\partial \zeta} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial \zeta}$
worin V das Potential, P den Druck im Punkte x, y, z zur Zeit t und $\varepsilon$ die Constante bezeichnet, welche die Anziehung zwischen zwei Masseneinheiten in der Entfernungseinheit ausdrückt.
Es handelt sich nun zunächst darum, die Grössen links vom Gleichheitszeichen in die Form [-...-] linearer[?] Functionen von den Grössen $\xi, \eta, \zeta$ zu setzen, wozu einige Vorbereitungen nöthig sind.
Durch Differentiation der Gleichungen 2) erhält man, wenn man zur Abkürzung
$\frac{dx}{dt}\alpha + \frac{dy}{dt}\beta + \frac{dz}{dt}\gamma = \xi'$
(2) $\frac{dx}{dt}\alpha' + \frac{dy}{dt}\beta' + \frac{dz}{dt}\gamma' = \eta'$
$\frac{dx}{dt}\alpha'' + \frac{dy}{dt}\beta'' + \frac{dz}{dt}\gamma'' = \zeta'$
setzt,
$\frac{\partial \xi}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial \alpha}{\partial t}x + \frac{\partial \beta}{\partial t}y + \frac{\partial \gamma}{\partial t}z + \xi'$
$\frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial \alpha'}{\partial t}x + \frac{\partial \beta'}{\partial t}y + \frac{\partial \gamma'}{\partial t}z + \eta'$
$\frac{\partial \zeta}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial \alpha''}{\partial t}x + \frac{\partial \beta''}{\partial t}y + \frac{\partial \gamma''}{\partial t}z + \zeta'$
und wenn man hierin x, y, z wieder durch $\xi, \eta, \zeta$ ausdrückt,
$\frac{\partial \xi}{\partial t} = (\frac{\partial \alpha}{\partial t}\alpha + \frac{\partial \beta}{\partial t}\beta + \frac{\partial \gamma}{\partial t}\gamma)\xi + (\frac{\partial \alpha}{\partial t}\alpha' + \frac{\partial \beta}{\partial t}\beta' + \frac{\partial \gamma}{\partial t}\gamma')\eta + (\frac{\partial \alpha}{\partial t}\alpha'' + \frac{\partial \beta}{\partial t}\beta'' + \frac{\partial \gamma}{\partial t}\gamma'')\zeta + \xi'$
$\frac{\partial \eta}{\partial t} = (\frac{\partial \alpha'}{\partial t}\alpha + \frac{\partial \beta'}{\partial t}\beta + \frac{\partial \gamma'}{\partial t}\gamma)\xi + (\frac{\partial \alpha'}{\partial t}\alpha' + \frac{\partial \beta'}{\partial t}\beta' + \frac{\partial \gamma'}{\partial t}\gamma')\eta + (\frac{\partial \alpha'}{\partial t}\alpha'' + \frac{\partial \beta'}{\partial t}\beta'' + \frac{\partial \gamma'}{\partial t}\gamma'')\zeta + \eta'$
$\frac{\partial \zeta}{\partial t} = (\frac{\partial \alpha''}{\partial t}\alpha + \frac{\partial \beta''}{\partial t}\beta + \frac{\partial \gamma''}{\partial t}\gamma)\xi + (\frac{\partial \alpha''}{\partial t}\alpha' + \frac{\partial \beta''}{\partial t}\beta' + \frac{\partial \gamma''}{\partial t}\gamma')\eta + (\frac{\partial \alpha''}{\partial t}\alpha'' + \frac{\partial \beta''}{\partial t}\beta'' + \frac{\partial \gamma''}{\partial t}\gamma'')\zeta + \zeta'$
Nun [-ist aber in Folge-] {+giebt aber die Differentiation+} der bekannten Gleichungen $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2 = 1$, $\alpha\alpha'+\beta\beta'+\gamma\gamma' = 0$, &c.
$\alpha\frac{\partial \alpha}{\partial t} + \beta\frac{\partial \beta}{\partial t} + \gamma\frac{\partial \gamma}{\partial t} = 0$ $\alpha'\frac{\partial \alpha'}{\partial t} + \beta'\frac{\partial \beta'}{\partial t} + \gamma'\frac{\partial \gamma'}{\partial t} = 0$ $\alpha''\frac{\partial \alpha''}{\partial t} + \beta''\frac{\partial \beta''}{\partial t} + \gamma''\frac{\partial \gamma''}{\partial t} = 0$
$\frac{\partial \alpha'}{\partial t}\alpha'' + \frac{\partial \beta'}{\partial t}\beta'' + \frac{\partial \gamma'}{\partial t}\gamma'' = -(\frac{\partial \alpha''}{\partial t}\alpha' + \frac{\partial \beta''}{\partial t}\beta' + \frac{\partial \gamma''}{\partial t}\gamma')$
(3) $\frac{\partial \alpha''}{\partial t}\alpha + \frac{\partial \beta''}{\partial t}\beta + \frac{\partial \gamma''}{\partial t}\gamma = -(\frac{\partial \alpha}{\partial t}\alpha'' + \frac{\partial \beta}{\partial t}\beta'' + \frac{\partial \gamma}{\partial t}\gamma'')$
$\frac{\partial \alpha}{\partial t}\alpha' + \frac{\partial \beta}{\partial t}\beta' + \frac{\partial \gamma}{\partial t}\gamma' = -(\frac{\partial \alpha'}{\partial t}\alpha + \frac{\partial \beta'}{\partial t}\beta + \frac{\partial \gamma'}{\partial t}\gamma)$

methods.what: Equations of motion (Lagrangian form) projected onto rotating axes ξ, η, ζ with gravitational potential and pressure
Velocity components relative to the moving axes defined by projection
Time derivative of moving coordinates via derivatives of direction cosines
Orthogonality relations of rotation matrix differentiated: skew-symmetry of Ṙ R^T (angular velocity matrix)

items.quote: Offenbar ist es erlaubt, in jenen Gleichungen, statt der Derivirten nach den Anfangswerthen der Grössen x, y, z, welche dort durch a, b, c bezeichnet sind, die Derivirten nach den Grössen $\xi, \eta, \zeta$ zu setzen; denn die hiedurch gebildeten Gleichungen lassen sich als Aggregate von jenen darstellen und umgekehrt.
items.english: Obviously it is permitted, in those equations, instead of the derivatives with respect to the initial values of x, y, z (denoted there by a, b, c), to use the derivatives with respect to ξ, η, ζ; for the equations so formed can be represented as aggregates of those and conversely.

items.quote: Es handelt sich nun zunächst darum, die Grössen links vom Gleichheitszeichen in die Form [-...-] linearer[?] Functionen von den Grössen $\xi, \eta, \zeta$ zu setzen, wozu einige Vorbereitungen nöthig sind.
items.english: The task now is first to put the quantities on the left of the equals sign into the form of linear functions of ξ, η, ζ, for which some preparations are necessary.
